chapter: Arranging career and the JPJ Quartet
title: Other writing: Goodman, Harry James, Basie and the Jazz Repertory Company
summary: Budd names more bandleaders, his year and a half with Goodman, the New York Jazz Repertory Company and his 1961 Basie stint.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: -- of the things Benny Goodman played with his sextet when he and Teddy Wilson and Gene Krupa were all in the band. And I wrote for Benny Goodman's orchestra because I played with Benny Goodman's orchestra about a year and a half and I was doing some arranging for that. And I wrote for Harry James' orchestra when he first started out, when he left Benny Goodman to go on his own. And he went to Philadelphia to open up there and then I'm doing some writing now and also one of the [ASSOCIATE] directors and arrangers for the New York Jazz Repertory Company, and I sit in on some of their planning committees and some of the planning that they're doing for '75. I was with them in '74. And I wrote for Count Basie's orchestra while I was in Basie's orchestra --
